mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2% in the past month signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for returns remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL index exceeds 2.5%, signaling rising inflation expectations, S&P 500 forward returns turn negative over the next 5 trading days due to market uncertainty and risk aversion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite CPIAUCSL crossing above 2.5%, or t-test p-value >0.05 in such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in GDPC1 (demand) by over 5% and a decline in INDPRO (supply) by over 3% in the previous month creates a demand-supply imbalance, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as investors anticipate sustained growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >5% and INDPRO decreases by >3% in the last month
failure_condition: Rank IC for returns <0.03 over any 3-year window when both conditions are met, or returns not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (rising FEDFUNDS rates), S&P 500 forward returns turn negative over the next 20 days as higher interest rates reduce discounted cash flows and dampen equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during tightening periods, or t-test p-value >0.05 in such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE rises above 4.5%, signaling labor market weakness, S&P 500 returns become negative over the next 60 days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings pressures.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite UNRATE crossing above 4.5%, or p-value >0.05 in such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in labor demand (PAYEMS) and overall demand (RSAFS) both rising by over 10% and 5% respectively in the last month creates a virtuous cycle, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as investors anticipate sustained growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% and RSAFS increases by >5% in the last month
failure_condition: Rank IC for returns <0.03 over any 3-year window when both conditions are met, or returns not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (a demand indicator) exceeds 1000 units, signaling strong consumer demand, S&P 500 forward returns become positive over the next 5 days as market anticipates continued growth and investment.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-positive despite HOUST exceeding 1000, or p-value >0.05 in such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion characterized by high demand (GDPC1) and accommodative monetary policy (low FEDFUNDS), S&P 500 returns turn positive over the next 60 days as investors anticipate sustained growth and higher valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >5% and FEDFUNDS decreases by >1% in the last month
failure_condition: Rank IC for returns <0.03 over any 3-year window when both conditions are met, or returns not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).
